justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue: every R4-valid Patient candidate remains allowed in R6, and the added Group target only creates R6-to-R4 representability risk.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Extension or profile-based handling can mitigate exchange with R4 systems, but it is a down-conversion/backport strategy rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--allowing enrollment requests for a group of subjects--is reasonable and is directly reflected in the R6 target-profile widening plus updated `candidate` definition. Because the base R6 change preserves existing R4-valid `EnrollmentRequest.candidate` instances, the level of R4-to-R6 breakage is effectively none; the remaining concern is reverse-direction compatibility when R6 Group candidates are sent to R4 systems.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable for the R4-to-R6 direction, because the R6 design already preserves the R4 Patient-only target as a subset. Keeping Group support out of the base resource and using an extension or profile could ease R6-to-R4 exchange, but that would be a mitigation for older receivers and would weaken uniform core validation and discoverability of group enrollment in R6.
